messages:
Elaine: Quick q — how should we map burst credits to plan tiers (free / pro / enterprise)? Also: per-org vs per-key enforcement and how that shows up in the Console.
Sam: My take: default to per-org. Easier for customers with many API keys and simpler enforcement. Per-key as an enterprise opt-in.
Priya: Agree per-org for defaults, but enterprise often asks for per-key/team isolation. We should support both, not just one. UX needs to make the override explicit.
Jin: Implementation idea: enforcement layer checks org counter first, then key override if present. Headers: `X-RW-ORG`, `X-RW-KEY`. Gateway pseudocode:
```
if org_quota.available > 0:
  consume(org_quota)
else if key_quota and key_quota.available > 0:
  consume(key_quota)
else:
  reject(429)
```
Sam: Also: what refill model? We currently use a token-bucket in runtime. Sliding-window would be more accurate for some customers but heavier. Token-bucket seems fine for burst handling.
Priya: Suggestion for default burst sizes for Console copy (draft): free = 5_000 burst tokens/day, pro = 50_000/day, enterprise = negotiable (can request per-key slabs). Those tokens should be visible as "Burst credits remaining" next to the rate charts.
Elaine: UX: show two metrics: 1) steady-state rate limit (req/s) and 2) burst credits (tokens left, refill rate). Tooltip explaining "burst = short-term extra capacity to absorb spikes; refills daily at 00:00 org timezone".
Sam: Perf concern: if we allow both org and key counters, concurrent requests might double-deduct if not transactional. Need atomic increments in Redis or the counter store. Also think about eventual consistency for multi-region.
Jin: We'll implement counters in Redis with Lua script for atomic check-and-decrement. Example script (sketch):
```
local o = tonumber(redis.call('GET', org_key) or 0)
local k = tonumber(redis.call('GET', key_key) or 0)
if o > 0 then
  redis.call('DECR', org_key)
  return 'org'
elseif k > 0 then
  redis.call('DECR', key_key)
  return 'key'
else
  return 'none'
end
```
Priya: Telemetry: we need events `quota.burst.used`, `quota.burst.refilled`, `quota.exceeded` with fields: org_id, key_id (optional), plan_tier, consumed_tokens, reason. Add these to the schema so product can build charts.
Elaine: Console/workflow: admin can set `default_scope: org` and add overrides per-key. The plan mapping table should look like: `free -> 5k/day, pro -> 50k/day, enterprise -> custom`. Make sure docs explain billing implication: burst tokens are free (don't increment billing) but if customers consistently consume > steady-state we'll recommend upgrading or customizing slab.
Sam: Edge case: burst consumption across multiple endpoints (completion vs embeddings) — we should either have a unified token or per-resource tokens. I'd vote unified burst pool per org to keep UX simple.
Priya: For enterprise, allow per-resource breakdown as an opt-in feature.
quota-bot: Rule change recorded by quota-admin: "Add burst slab defaults for free/pro and per-key override flag" — link: https://go/repo/changes/745
Jin: I'll pick this up. I'll add gateway check, Lua script, and unit tests for concurrency. Also add canary config in deploys for eng-platform.
Elaine: Assignments: Jin = implementation + tests, Priya = Console mockups + telemetry schema, Sam = perf tests + Redis/Lua review. ETA?
Jin: ETA EOW for initial PR, canary early next week. :thumbsup:
Sam: I'll add perf harness and start load tests tomorrow.
Priya: I'll drop mockups in Figma and a short doc for Console copy.
Elaine: Sounds good. One more: we should add a small notice in the signup flow explaining free plan burst limits to reduce surprise.
quota-bot: quota-bot: scheduled task: create analytics dashboard `Quota -> Burst Usage` (owner: Priya)
